ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The first verse concerns baseless deities: they are themselves created and have created nothing, making their worship foolish.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: those whom they worship are themselves created and have created nothing. Worshipping them is foolishness.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r4.claim: Most readers use second-person ت in the three verbs, with the named readers following that address form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: بالتاء من فوق في تسرون وتعلنون وتدعون، وهي قراءة: مجاهد، والأعرج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r5.speaker: عاصم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r5.claim: In his well-known reading, Asim has third-person ي in يدعون while retaining second-person ت in the two preceding verbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r5.anchor: وقرأ عاصم في مشهوره: يدعون بالياء من تحت، وبالتاء في السابقتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r6.speaker: الأعمش وأصحاب عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Ibn Masud's companions read يعلم الذي يبدون وما يكتمون and use second-person ت in تدعون throughout.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r6.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش وأصحاب عبد الله: يعلم الذي يبدون وما يكتمون، وتدعون بالتاء من فوق في الثلاثة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r7.speaker: طلحة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r7.claim: Talha reads ما يخفون وما يعلنون and uses second-person ت in تدعون.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r7.anchor: وقرأ طلحة: ما يخفون وما يعلنون، وتدعون بالتاء من فوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r8.claim: The al-Aʿmash and Talha forms diverge from the codex consonantal text and should be treated as explanatory readings, not Qur'an.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r8.anchor: وهاتان القراءتان مخالفتان لسواد المصحف، والمشهور ما روي عن الأعمش وغيره، فوجب حملها على التفسير، لا على أنها قرآن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r9.claim: Idols neither create nor live; the added phrase غير أحياء stresses their death, and they lack even animal awareness, much less rational knowledge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r9.anchor: نص على أن آلهتهم لا تخلق، وعلى أنها مخلوقة. وأخبر أنهم أموات، وأكد ذلك بقوله: غير أحياء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r10.claim: The relative pronoun for rational beings is applied to idols because people worshiped them and believed them divine.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r10.anchor: وعبر بالذين وهو للعاقل عومل غيره معاملته، لكونها عبدت واعتقدت فيها الألوهية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r11.speaker: محمد اليماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r11.claim: Muhammad al-Yamani reads يدعون with passive morphology.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r11.anchor: وقرأ محمد اليماني: يدعون بضم الياء وفتح العين مبنيا للمفعول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r12.claim: The apparent reading says God created the idols; al-Zamakhshari alternatively says people carve and shape them, leaving them more helpless than their worshipers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن قوله: وهم يخلقون، أي: الله أنشأهم واخترعهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhshari's alternative is that people make idols by carving and shaping, while the idols cannot do likewise.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p517/r13.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ووجه آخر وهو أن يكون المعنى: أن الناس يخلقونهم بالنحت والتصوير

ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r3.claim: The reading of ‘those you invoke’ varies between second-person plural tadʿūna and third-person plural yudʿawna.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r3.anchor: ويقرأ (تدعون من دون الله) بالتاء والياء.

ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r4.claim: The verse refers to the idols worshipped by the Arabs: they create nothing and are themselves created.
ZAJJAJ:v3p193#2/r4.anchor: يعنى به الأوثان التي كانت تعبدها العرب.

SAMIN-DURR:16:20/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:16:20/r1.speaker: عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:16:20/r1.claim: Asim alone reads يدعون with yāʾ; the other readers use tāʾ. A passive reading is also transmitted; the author says the variants are clear.
SAMIN-DURR:16:20/r1.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحده " يدعون " بالياء، والباقون بالتاء من فوق. وقرئ " يدعون " مبنيا للمفعول

ASAD-NOTES:16:20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:20/r1.claim: Those invoked beside God are themselves created and cannot create anything.
ASAD-NOTES:16:20/r1.anchor: Now those beings that some people invoke [13] beside God cannot create anything, since they themselves are but created

ASAD-NOTES:16:20#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:20#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:20#n13/r1.claim: The invoked beings are dead saints whom followers have given divine or semi-divine qualities.
ASAD-NOTES:16:20#n13/r1.anchor: this refers - as is obvious from verse 21 below - to dead saints invested by their followers with divine or semi-divine qualities

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p210/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p210/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p210/r1.claim: The clause is read with tāʾ or yāʾ, as in a previously explained parallel reading.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p210/r1.anchor: يقرآن بالتاء والياء وقد تقدم من القول في مثاله ما يغني عن إعادته

QIRAAT-ER:16:20:3#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:16:20:3#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:16:20:3#1/r1.claim: The second-person plural reading means “those whom you call upon,” addressing the audience directly and making the accusation personal.
QIRAAT-ER:16:20:3#1/r1.anchor: Imp, mutawatir: "2nd person masculine plural: ""those whom YOU (yourselves) call upon

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r1.claim: The passage begins showing that the worshipped gods are plainly unfit for worship; spelling out their obvious defects exposes the idolaters' folly.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r1.anchor: شروع في تحقيق أن آلهتهم بمعزل عن استحقاق العبادة وتوضيحه بحيث لا يبقى فيه شائبة ريب

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r2.claim: The deities worshipped apart from God create absolutely nothing; creating anything is not among their attributes.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r3.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r3.claim: One explanation connects this to the preceding denial of likeness: since noncreators do not share in creating with the Creator, the conclusion that they are unlike Him follows without repetition.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r3.anchor: وذكر بعض الأجلة أن ذكر هذا بعد نفي التشابه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r4.speaker: قيل عليه
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r4.claim: An objection says the preceding reasoning already specifies God as creator and idols as noncreators, making the inference unnecessary; the repetition instead pairs with their being created.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#2/r4.anchor: إنه مبني على أن من يخلق ومن لا مجرى على غير معين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r1.claim: Alusi answers that creator and noncreator are stated universally, though their contextual referents are God and idols; the earlier premise is so evident that it can still serve in the proof.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r1.anchor: المصرح به العموم في الموضعين وأما التخصيص فيهما بما ذكر فلأن من يخلق عندنا مخصوص به تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r2.claim: Alusi says the better explanation for mentioning createdness is the pairing already indicated, rather than treating the repetition as redundant.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r2.anchor: ولعل الأوجه في توجيه الذكر ما أشرنا إليه أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r3.claim: Noncreation alone does not entail createdness, so the verse states it explicitly: their possible natures depend on an agent for existence and continuance.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r3.anchor: وحيث أنه لا تلازم أصلا بين نفي الخالقية وبين المخلوقية أثبت ذلك لهم صريحا

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r4.speaker: بعض الأجلة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r4.claim: The passive voice sharpens the contrast between the denied quality of creating and the affirmed quality of being created, while leaving the agent unstated because God is obvious.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r4.anchor: وبناء الفعل للمفعول كما قال بعض الأجلة لتحقيق التضاد والمقابلة بين ما أثبت لهم وما نفي عنهم

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r5.claim: The pronoun is placed first for emphasis, and both instances of creation retain their ordinary meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r5.anchor: ولعل تقديم الضمير هنا لمجرد التقوى والمراد بالخلق منفيا ومثبتا المعنى المتبادر منه

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r6.claim: Another reading takes the second creation as carving or shaping the idols, using rational language for them by treating them as rational and by rhetorical matching; applying this to the first creation is invalid because idol-making does not establish worthiness of worship.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r6.anchor: وجوز أن يراد من الثاني النحت والتصوير بناء على أن المراد من الذين يدعونهم الأصنام

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r7.speaker: الجمهور ومجاهد والأعرج وشيبة وأبو جعفر وهبيرة عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r7.claim: The majority and the named readers read the surrounding verbs تسرون وتعلنون وتدعون with second-person tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بالتاء المثناة من فوق

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r8.speaker: عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r8.claim: In the well-known transmission from ʿĀṣim, the final تدعون is read with third-person yāʾ, while the first two verbs retain tāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r8.anchor: وفي المشهور عنه أنه قرأ بالياء آخر الحروف في الأخير وبالتاء في الأولين

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r9.claim: A transmission from Abu ʿAmr and Hamza reads all three surrounding verbs with third-person yāʾ.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r9.anchor: وقرئت الثلاثة بالياء في رواية عن أبي عمرو وحمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r10.speaker: الأعمش وطلحة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r10.claim: Al-Aʿmash and Talha have explanatory variants with tāʾ in all three verbs; Alusi says these readings are interpretive because they diverge from the codex consonantal text.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r10.anchor: بالتاء من فوق في الأفعال الثلاث

ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r11.speaker: محمد اليماني
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r11.claim: Muhammad al-Yamani reads يدعون in the passive, meaning the idols are summoned by the disbelievers and worshipped.
ALUSI-FULL:v14p119#3/r11.anchor: بضم الياء وفتح العين مبنيا للمفعول

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r4.claim: Those invoked apart from God are idols.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r4.anchor: {والذين يدعون من دون الله} يعني: الأصنام،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r5.speaker: عاصم ويعقوب
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim and Yaʿqūb read yadʿūn with yāʾ.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r6.claim: Idols create nothing, are themselves created, and are dead rather than living.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p14/r6.anchor: لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون} {أموات} أي: الأصنام

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r1.claim: Those invoked besides God are the deities people worship.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r1.anchor: { والذين يدعون من دون الله } أي والآلهة الذين تعبدونهم من دونه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r2.speaker: أبو بكر وحفص
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r2.claim: Abū Bakr reads yadʿūn with yāʾ; Ḥafṣ reads all three occurrences in this passage with yāʾ.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر «يدعون» بالياء. وقرأ حفص ثلاثتها بالياء.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r3.claim: Because these deities create nothing, they cannot share God’s divinity; as contingent beings they depend on creation, whereas a deity must exist necessarily.
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:20/r3.anchor: لما نفى المشاركة بين من يخلق ومن لا يخلق بين أنهم لا يخلقون شيئا لينتج أنهم لا يشاركونه

BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r4.claim: Those invoked besides God are worshipped idols.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r4.anchor: أي دعاء عبادة { من دون الله } أي الذي له جميع صفات الكمال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r5.claim: God alone has perfect power, knowledge and creation; idols cannot create anything and are themselves created, so they cannot be divine.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p256/r5.anchor: ولما أثبت لنفسه تعالى كمال القدرة وتمام العلم وأنه المنفرد بالخلق , شرع يقيم الأدلة

BURSEVI:v5p18/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p18/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p18/r1.claim: Those invoked are the gods worshipped by unbelievers; in Quranic usage, calling upon a deity often means worshipping it.
BURSEVI:v5p18/r1.anchor: أي : والآلهة الذين يعبدهم الكفار والدعاء بمعنى العبادة

BURSEVI:v5p18/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p18/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p18/r2.claim: Min dūni Allāh is circumstantial and means going beyond God; dūn first means a lower place, then difference in rank and broadly crossing a boundary or rule.
BURSEVI:v5p18/r2.anchor: نصب على الحال أي : متجاوزين الله فإن معنى دون أدنى مكان

BURSEVI:v5p18/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p18/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p18/r3.claim: The idols create nothing because creation is not within their capacity and they are powerless.
BURSEVI:v5p18/r3.anchor: أي : ليس من شأنهم ذلك لأنهم عجزة

BURSEVI:v5p18/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p18/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p18/r4.claim: Createdness is intrinsic to the idols, since contingent beings depend on a creator for their essence and existence.
BURSEVI:v5p18/r4.anchor: أي : شأنهم ومقتضى ذاتهم المخلوقية لأنها ذوات ممكنة مفتقرة

BURSEVI:v5p18/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p18/r5.speaker: القاموس
BURSEVI:v5p18/r5.claim: Al-Qāmūs defines the Creator as the one who originates and invents a thing without a prior model.
BURSEVI:v5p18/r5.anchor: قال في "القاموس" : الخالق في صفاته المبدع للشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r1.claim: This clause is conjoined to the denial of equality in 16:17 and to the statement in 16:19 that God knows what people conceal.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r2.claim: Those invoked besides God are the idols; the address here focuses on the polytheists, a subset of the earlier addressees.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r2.anchor: ظاهر أن الخطاب هنا متمحض للمشركين وهم بعض المخاطبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r3.claim: This passage explicitly states the idols' lack of creative power and knowledge, which the preceding arguments had already implied.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r3.anchor: والمقصود من هذه الجملة التصريح بما استفيد ضمنا مما قبلها وهو نفي الخالقية ونفي العلم عن الأصنام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r4.claim: The denial that idols create anything makes explicit the implication of the earlier question about creator and noncreator.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r5.claim: Saying that they themselves are created advances the proof against their divinity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r5.anchor: ارتقاء في الاستدلال على انتفاء إلهيتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r6.claim: The implied creator is God: idols are made of stones created by Him, and human carving does not change that origin, as 37:96 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p125/r6.anchor: فإنهم من الحجارة التي هي من خلق الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p126/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p126/r1.speaker: عاصم ويعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p126/r1.claim: Asim and Yaqub read with third-person yāʾ; Ibn ʿĀshūr says this clarifies that the majority reading addresses the polytheists.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r6.claim: The idols are called ‘who’ for two reasons: the verse rebuts every form of worship besides God, and the expression uses ‘who’ for categories apt to receive that reference.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r6.anchor: وعبر عن الأصنام ب «من» لوجهين، أحدهما أن الآية تضمنت الرد على جميع من عبد غير الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r7.claim: The second reason is that the wording follows the unbelievers’ belief that their idols have influence and agency.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r7.anchor: والآخر أن العبارة جرت في الأصنام بحسب اعتقاد الكفرة فيها في أن لها تأثيرا وأفعالا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r19.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r19.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r19.claim: ‘You call’ means that they call the idols gods; ‘those who’ includes idols, everything worshipped besides God, and other referents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r19.anchor: تدعون معناه تدعونه إلها، وعبر عن الأصنام ب الذين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r20.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r20.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r20.claim: The statement that idols neither create nor escape being created is a comprehensive denial of their divine attributes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p385/r20.anchor: وقوله تعالى: لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون أجمع عبارة في نفي أحوال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p386/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p386/r1.speaker: محمد اليماني
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p386/r1.claim: Muḥammad al-Yamānī reads the opening verb passively, with ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on ʿayn.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p386/r1.anchor: وقرأ محمد اليماني «والذين يدعون» بضم الياء وفتح على ما لم يسم.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437#4/r1.speaker: عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p437#4/r1.claim: Asim reads yadʿūn with yāʾ, rather than the second-person form.

JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم ويعقوب الحضرمي
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r2.claim: Abū Bakr reads يدعون in the third person but addresses the listeners directly in تسرون and تعلنون; Yaʿqūb reads the latter forms this way too.
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: والذين يدعون بالياء خاصة على المعاينة و تسرون وتعلنون بالتاء على الخطاب وهو قراءة يعقوب الحضرمي

JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r3.speaker: الباقون
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r3.claim: The remaining readers use direct-address tāʾ for all three verbs, continuing the preceding address.
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ الباقون كلها بالتاء على الخطاب على ما قبله.

JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r8.claim: The clause ends at وهم يخلقون; أموات begins a new sentence, understood as “they are dead,” and أيان is an accusative time adverb.
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r8.anchor: تم الكلام عند قوله: (وهم يخلقون) ثم ابتدأ فقال: (أموات) أي: هم أموات، ونصب أيان لأنه ظرف

JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r9.claim: After establishing God's power and favors as Creator, the passage directly argues against worshiping anything besides Him.
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r9.anchor: لما تقدم الدعاء إلى عبادته تعالى ببيان قدرته ونعمته، وأنه خالق الأشياء خاطب في هذه الآية المشركين

JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r11.claim: Those invoked apart from God are the idols.
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r11.anchor: والذين يدعون من دون الله أي: تدعونه إلها، وهو الأصنام

JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r12.claim: Idols neither create nor benefit or harm; as originated things they require an originator, and bodies require a maker unlike bodies, establishing God as Creator.
JISHUMI:v6p4013#2/r12.anchor: لأنهم محدثون فلا بد لهم من محدث صانع، وإذا كان القادر بالقدرة لا يصح منه خلق الجواهر والأجسام فلا بد لها من صانع مخالف للأجسام

MUQATIL:16:20-22/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:20-22/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:20-22/r1.claim: Those worshipped besides God by Meccan unbelievers are al-Lat, al-Uzza, Manat, and Hubal.

MUQATIL:16:20-22/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:20-22/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:20-22/r2.claim: The idols create nothing, not even a fly, and are themselves carved by their worshippers' hands.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r1.claim: Those the unbelievers call upon apart from God are the idols.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r1.anchor: يدعوهم الكفار ﴿ من دون الله ﴾ وبالتاء غير عاصم

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r2.claim: All readers other than ʿĀṣim read the verb with tāʾ.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p252#6/r3.claim: The idols create nothing and are themselves created.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r1.claim: Most readers have تدعون with tāʾ, matching the preceding address; Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim and Hubayra from Ḥafṣ read يدعون with yāʾ, as does Yaʿqūb.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والذين يدعون من دون الله } قراءة العامة «تدعون» بالتاء لأن ما قبله خطاب. روى أبو بكر عن عاصم وهبيرة عن حفص «يدعون» بالياء،

QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r2.claim: All read the phrase with tāʾ-address except Hubayra’s report from Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, which has yāʾ.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r2.anchor: { ما تسرون وما تعلنون } فكلهم بالتاء على الخطاب إلا ما روى هبيرة عن حفص عن عاصم أنه قرأ بالياء.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r3.claim: The idols have no power to create anything.
QURTUBI-FULL:16:20-21/r3.anchor: { لا يخلقون شيئا } أي لا يقدرون على خلق شيء { وهم يخلقون }.

RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim reads the three verbs ‘they conceal, reveal, and call upon’ with third-person yāʾ throughout.
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r1.anchor: قرأ حفص عن عاصم يسرون ويعلنون ويدعون كلها بالياء

RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r2.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r2.claim: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim reads يدعون in the third person but تسرون and تعلنون in the second person.
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r2.anchor: يدعون } بالياء خاصة على المغايبة وتسرون وتعلنون بالتاء على الخطاب

RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r3.speaker: الباقون
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r3.claim: The remaining readers use second-person tāʾ forms throughout, coordinating these verbs with the preceding address.
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r3.anchor: والباقون كلها بالتاء على الخطاب عطفا على ما قبله

RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r4.claim: The second phrase adds that idols are themselves created by another, beyond the preceding statement that they create nothing; both expose their deficiencies.
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r4.anchor: أنهم لا يخلقون شيئا وأنهم مخلوقون لغيرهم ، فكان هذا زيادة في المعنى

RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r5.claim: The idols are dead rather than living; a true deity must be alive without ever dying, whereas idols have the opposite condition.
RAZI-FULL:v20p13#2/r5.anchor: لو كانت آلهة على الحقيقة لكانوا أحياء غير أموات ، أي غير جائز عليها الموت

STUDYQURAN:16:20/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:20/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:20/r1.claim: Idols are created, unlike God, who is uncreated; 37:95–96 likewise contrasts carved idols with God, who created the people and their handiwork.
STUDYQURAN:16:20/r1.anchor: That the idols are “created” presents an additional contrast with God, Who is “uncreated”

TABRISI:16:20-22/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:20-22/r1.speaker: عاصم غير الأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر ويعقوب وسهل
TABRISI:16:20-22/r1.claim: ʿĀṣim apart from al-Aʿshā and al-Barjamī through Abū Bakr, plus Yaʿqūb and Sahl, read with yāʾ.
TABRISI:16:20-22/r1.anchor: القراءة: { والذين يدعون } بالياء عن عاصم غير الأعشى والبرجمي عن أبي بكر

TABRISI:16:20-22/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:20-22/r2.speaker: الباقون
TABRISI:16:20-22/r2.claim: The other readers use tāʾ, continuing surrounding direct address.

TABRISI:16:20-22/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:20-22/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:20-22/r3.claim: The tāʾ reading follows surrounding address; the yāʾ reading turns to the Prophet and reports about the idolaters.
TABRISI:16:20-22/r3.anchor: من قرأ بالتاء فلأن ما بعده وما قبله خطاب

TABRISI:16:20-22/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:20-22/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:20-22/r4.claim: After inviting worship through blessings and power, the passage notes God's knowledge of intentions, then invalidates association in worship.
TABRISI:16:20-22/r4.anchor: لما قدم سبحانه الدعاء إلى عبادته بذكر نعمه وكمال قدرته

TABRISI:16:20-22/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:20-22/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:20-22/r6.claim: Those invoked beside God are idols, unable to create and fashioned from created stone, wood, and similar materials.
TABRISI:16:20-22/r6.anchor: يعني الأصنام لا يمكنها خلق شيء بل هي مخلوقة مربوبة منحوتة من الحجر والخشب

THALABI:v6p12#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p12#2/r1.claim: The common reading has the second-person tāʾ, matching the preceding address; Yaʿqūb, ʿĀṣim, and Sahl read the third-person yāʾ.
THALABI:v6p12#2/r1.anchor: قرأه العامة بالتاء، لأن ما قبله كله خطاب. وقرأ يعقوب وعاصم وسهل بالياء.

THALABI:v6p12#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p12#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p12#2/r2.claim: The beings invoked besides God create nothing themselves; rather, they are created.
THALABI:v6p12#2/r2.anchor: لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون ثم وصف الأوثان فقال

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p38#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p38#2/r1.speaker: عاصم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p38#2/r1.claim: The general reading has the second-person form taʾ, matching the preceding address to disbelievers; Asim reads yaʾ, reporting about the polytheists who worship idols, then describing those idols.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p38#2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {والذين يدعون} قراءة العامة بالتاء (¬6)؛ لأن ما قبل هذه الآية كلها خطاب للكفار، وقرأ عاصم بالياء في: {يدعون} (¬7)

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r1.claim: Those invoked besides God are idols.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r2.claim: The idols create nothing; people fashion the idols by hand, as the passage about what people carve also illustrates.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r3.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r3.claim: Al-Suddī explains that the idols are fashioned into images.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p57/r3.anchor: وقال السدي: {لا يخلقون شيئا وهم يخلقون} [النحل: 20] ، يعني: وهم يصورون.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r1.speaker: eski tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r1.claim: The common early interpretation, preferred in the translation, is that the idols are lifeless: since life is a basic divine attribute, it is irrational to seek help and salvation from an inanimate object.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r1.anchor: Eski tefsirlerdeki yaygın yorum bizim meâlde tercih ettiğimiz şekildedir. Çünkü tanrılığın, temel niteliklerinin başında hayat sıfatı gelir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r2.speaker: ikinci yorum
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r2.claim: A second reading says people carve the idols, which cannot create and are more helpless than their makers; how could such things know the time of resurrection when humans do not know it?
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r2.anchor: İkinci bir yorum da şöyledir: Bazı nesneleri yontarak, şekillendirerek put haline getiren insanlardır. Oysa putlar böyle bir şey yapıp yaratmaya muktedir değildir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r3.claim: Another proposed referent is the angels whom polytheists worshipped or prayed to as God's daughters and assigned divine functions; the phrase that they are dead means that angels, like people, are mortal.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r3.anchor: Burada müşriklerin taptıkları veya dua ve niyazda bulundukları şeylerin melekler olabileceği de düşünülmüştür. Çünkü müşrikler, melekleri Allah’ın kızları sayarak onlara tanrısal fonksiyonlar yüklerlerdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r4.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports a figurative reading in which the dead and lifeless are the unbelievers: disbelief is like death because it is heedlessness and lack of reason.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r4.anchor: inkâr sapkınlığıdır; çünkü inkâr, ölüm gibi bir şuursuzluk, akılsızlıktır (İbn Atıyye, III, 386)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r5.speaker: Ateş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r5.claim: Ateş proposes that the idols may be carved and erected symbols representing ancestors among the Arabs.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r5.anchor: Burada putların, Araplar’ca atalarını temsil ettiği için yontulmuş ve dikilmiş semboller olarak da anlaşılabileceği yorumu da yapılmıştır (Ateş, V, 97-98)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r6.claim: The author finds no evidence that pre-Islamic Arabs deified ancestor spirits, so he rejects this as a sufficient reason to displace the common early interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r6.anchor: İslâm öncesi Araplarının atalarıyla övündükleri bilinmekle birlikte ata ruhlarını tanrılaştırma (animizm) türü bir inanca sahip olduklarına dair herhangi bir bilgi bulunmamaktadır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r7.claim: The Qur'an personifies idols according to the polytheists' own reasoning, as in the later question asking where God's partners are; this supports retaining the common interpretation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:20/r7.anchor: Kur’an’ın, putları canlı ve şuurlu varlıklar sayan müşriklerin mantığıyla konuyu ele alan hâkim üslûbudur. Nitekim aşağıda 27. âyette “Hani ortaklarım nerede?” diye sorulurken de aynı mantıktan hareket edilmiştir

BURHAN:v1p118/r12.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p118/r12.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p118/r12.claim: Al-Naḥl says “those they call upon besides God,” while al-Aʿrāf uses “besides Him.”

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r1.speaker: ابن كثير، وأبو عمرو، ونافع، وابن عامر، وحمزة، والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r1.claim: These readers use tāʾ in all three verbs: ‘you conceal,’ ‘you disclose,’ and ‘those you call upon.’
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو ونافع وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي: (والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون والذين تدعون) كلهن بالتاء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r2.speaker: عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r2.claim: Asim reads the first two verbs with tāʾ but reads yadʿūna, ‘they call,’ with yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r2.anchor: وقرأ عاصم: والله يعلم ما تسرون وما تعلنون بالتاء، والذين يدعون بالياء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r3.speaker: حفص عن عاصم، عن هبيرة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r3.claim: Hafs, in the transmission through Hubeira, is reported to read all three verbs with yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r3.anchor: أخبرنا الخزاز عن هبيرة، عن حفص عن عاصم: أنه قرأهن ثلاثتهن بالياء.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r4.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r4.speaker: حفص عن عاصم، عن عمرو بن الصباح
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r4.claim: Another report from Hafs, through Amr ibn al-Sabbah, matches Abu Bakr from Asim: first two tāʾ, last yāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r4.anchor: وقال ابن اليتيم عن أبي حفص عمرو بن الصباح عن حفص عن عاصم مثل أبي بكر عن عاصم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r5.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r5.speaker: الكسائي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi transmits from Abu Bakr from Asim a reading with yāʾ in all three verbs.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r5.anchor: وروى الكسائي عن أبي بكر عن عاصم: ذلك كله بالياء في الثلاثة .

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r6.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r6.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r6.claim: The surrounding passage addresses listeners, including ‘Will you not remember?’ and the preceding references to 16:15 and 16:22; an implied qul also permits tāʾ in the clause about those invoked.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r6.anchor: هذا يكون كله على الخطاب، لأن ما بعده خطاب كقوله بعد: أفلا تذكرون. وقوله: وألقى في الأرض رواسي أن تميد بكم [النحل/ 15] وإلهكم إله واحد [النحل/ 22]،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r7.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r7.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r7.claim: Asim’s yāʾ marks the clause as information about the polytheists and their gods, rather than a direct address to the Prophet or Muslims.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r7.anchor: ولهذا قرأ عاصم: والذين يدعون بالياء، لما كان ذلك عنده إخبارا عن المشركين،

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r8.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r8.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r8.claim: An all-yāʾ reading can address the Prophet through an implied ‘Tell them’: God knows what they conceal and disclose, and those whom they invoke call upon no one.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p58/r8.anchor: فأما ما روي عن عاصم من أنه قرأ كله بالياء، فهذا على توجيه الخطاب إلى النبي صلى الله
